[Event-driven] When the daily transaction posting job executes, the system shall read each transaction record sequentially from the daily transactions file and, for each record, perform validation before determining whether to post or reject the transaction.
REQ-F-002

[Event-driven] When a transaction record is read from the daily transactions file and end-of-file is not yet reached, the system shall set the result to success (0); when end-of-file is encountered, the system shall set the result to 16 and terminate the processing loop; when any other read error occurs, the system shall set the result to 12.
REQ-F-003

[Event-driven] When a transaction record requires validation, the system shall look up the card number in the cross reference file; if the card number is not found, the system shall set the validation failure reason to 100.
REQ-F-004

[Event-driven] When the card number is found in the cross reference file, the system shall retrieve the associated account ID and look up the account record in the account data file; if the account record is not found, the system shall set the validation failure reason to 101.
REQ-F-005

[Event-driven] When the account record is found, the system shall compute a temporary balance as current cycle credit minus current cycle debit plus the transaction amount; if the credit limit is less than the temporary balance, the system shall set the validation failure reason to 102.
REQ-F-006

[Event-driven] When the account record is found and the credit limit check passes, the system shall compare the account expiration date against the first 10 characters (date portion) of the transaction's original timestamp; if the expiration date is earlier than the transaction date, the system shall set the validation failure reason to 103.
REQ-F-007
[Event-driven] When all validation checks pass, the system shall set the validation failure reason to 0.
REQ-F-008

[Event-driven] When a transaction fails validation, the system shall assemble a rejection record containing the original transaction data and the validation failure reason code and description, then write the rejection record to the daily rejection output file (daily rejection file, `DALYREJS-FILE`).
REQ-F-009
[Event-driven] When a transaction passes all validation checks, the system shall add the transaction amount to the current account balance in the account data file.
REQ-F-010

[Event-driven] When posting a valid transaction, if the transaction amount is greater than or equal to zero, the system shall add the transaction amount to the current cycle credit total on the account record.
REQ-F-011
[Event-driven] When posting a valid transaction, if the transaction amount is less than zero, the system shall add the transaction amount to the current cycle debit total on the account record.
REQ-F-012
[Event-driven] When the account balance and cycle totals have been updated, the system shall rewrite the updated account record to the account data file.
REQ-F-013

[Event-driven] When a valid transaction is posted, the system shall read the transaction category balance record from the transaction category balance file using the composite key of account ID, transaction type code, and transaction category code; if the record does not exist, the system shall create a new transaction category balance record populated with the account ID, transaction type code, transaction category code, and the transaction amount as the initial category balance.
REQ-F-014

[Event-driven] When the transaction category balance record already exists for the account ID, transaction type code, and transaction category code combination, the system shall add the transaction amount to the existing category balance and rewrite the updated record to the transaction category balance file.
REQ-F-015

[Event-driven] When a validated transaction is ready to be posted, the system shall copy all transaction details from the daily transaction record (including transaction ID, type code, category code, source, description, amount, merchant ID, merchant name, merchant city, merchant zip, card number, and original timestamp) to the transaction record, obtain the current processing timestamp formatted as a DB2-compatible ISO 8601 string, and store it in the transaction record's processing timestamp field.
REQ-F-016

[Event-driven] When a transaction record has been posted and account balances have been updated, the system shall write the assembled transaction record to the transaction file (transaction file data store, `TRANSACT-FILE`) to create a permanent record of the posted transaction.
REQ-F-017

[Ubiquitous] The system shall format the current processing timestamp by extracting year, month, day, hour, minute, second, and millisecond components, separating date components with hyphens, separating time components with periods, and setting the trailing field to '0000'.
REQ-F-018

[Ubiquitous] The system shall merge transaction records from the transaction backup store and the system-generated transaction store, sort the merged records by transaction ID in ascending order, and write the sorted result to the combined transaction store.
REQ-F-019

[Event-driven] When the sort and merge to the combined transaction store is complete, the system shall copy all sorted transaction records from the combined transaction store to the transaction master store, preserving the sort order established during consolidation.
REQ-F-020

[Ubiquitous] The system shall read transaction records from the backup transaction data store, filter to include only records where the processing date equals 2022-06-02, sort the filtered records by card number in ascending order, and write the sorted results to the daily transaction data store.
REQ-F-021
[Ubiquitous] The system shall exclude from the daily transactions file any transaction record whose processing date does not equal 2022-06-02.
REQ-F-022

[Ubiquitous] The system shall read transaction category balance records sequentially from the transaction category balance file, read account master records from the account data file using the account ID as the key, read card cross-reference records from the cross reference file using the account ID as the alternate key, and read interest rate records from the discount group file using a composite key of account group ID, transaction type code, and transaction category code.
REQ-F-023

[State-driven] While transaction category balance records remain available, the system shall detect an account break when the account ID in the current record differs from the last processed account ID.
REQ-F-024

[Event-driven] When an account break is detected and it is not the first record processed, the system shall add the accumulated total interest to the current account balance, reset the current cycle credit and current cycle debit totals to zero, and rewrite the updated account record to the account data file.
REQ-F-025

[Event-driven] When an account break is detected, the system shall reset the total interest accumulator to zero, store the current account ID as the last processed account, retrieve the account master record from the account data file, and retrieve the card cross-reference record from the cross reference file.
REQ-F-026

[Event-driven] When an account group ID, transaction type code, and transaction category code are provided for interest rate lookup, the system shall read the discount group record from the discount group file using those three values as a composite key; if the record is not found, the system shall set the account group ID to 'DEFAULT' and retrieve the default interest rate record using the same transaction type and category codes.
REQ-F-027

[Event-driven] When an interest rate is available for a transaction category, the system shall compute the monthly interest as (transaction category balance × interest rate) ÷ 1200 and add the result to the total interest accumulator for the account.
REQ-F-028

[Event-driven] When monthly interest has been computed for a transaction category, the system shall construct a transaction record with: a transaction ID formed by concatenating the parameter date and an incremented suffix; transaction type code '01'; transaction category code '05'; source set to 'System'; description set to 'Int. for a/c ' concatenated with the account ID; amount set to the computed monthly interest; merchant fields cleared; card number populated from the cross reference record; and original and processing timestamps set to the current system date and time in ISO 8601 format with hyphens as date separators, periods as time separators, and the suffix '0000' appended.
REQ-F-029

[Event-driven] When a transaction record has been constructed for a monthly interest charge, the system shall write that record to the transaction category balance file's corresponding output — the transaction file opened in output mode.
REQ-F-030

[Event-driven] When end of file is reached on the transaction category balance file, the system shall apply the final account update by adding the accumulated total interest to the current account balance, resetting the current cycle credit and current cycle debit totals to zero, and rewriting the account record to the account data file.
REQ-F-031

[Event-driven] When a read of the transaction category balance file returns an end-of-file condition, the system shall set the result code to 16 and set the end-of-file flag to 'Y'; if any other error condition occurs during the read, the system shall set the result code to 12.

reqF: REQ-F-001

[Ubiquitous] The system shall capture the current calendar date and clock time at the start of the export run and format them into a single 26-character run timestamp of the form `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.00`, where the date components are separated by hyphens, the time components are separated by colons, a single space separates the date and time portions, and the fixed suffix `.00` is appended; this timestamp shall be shared by every record written during the run.
REQ-F-002

[Ubiquitous] The system shall open the customer input data store, account input data store, cross-reference input data store, transaction input data store, and card input data store for reading, and the export output data store for writing, before any records are exported.
REQ-F-003

[Ubiquitous] The system shall export records from the five source stores in the following fixed order: customers, accounts, card cross-references, transactions, and cards, using the shared run timestamp and a single shared sequence counter across all five export phases.
REQ-F-004

[State-driven] While records remain in the customer input data store, the system shall read each customer record sequentially and emit one customer export record per customer until the end of the customer input data store is reached.
REQ-F-005

[Event-driven] When a customer record has been read from the customer input data store, the system shall assemble an export record with record type `'C'`, the shared run timestamp, the next sequence number, originating branch `'0001'`, region `'NORTH'`, and the customer's identity fields, name components, three address lines, state, country, ZIP, two phone numbers, SSN, government-issued identifier, date of birth, EFT account number, primary-cardholder indicator, and FICO credit score, then write the assembled record to the export output data store.
REQ-F-006

[State-driven] While records remain in the account input data store, the system shall read each account record sequentially and emit one account export record per account until the end of the account input data store is reached.
REQ-F-007

[Event-driven] When an account record has been read from the account input data store, the system shall assemble an export record with record type `'A'`, the shared run timestamp, the next sequence number, originating branch `'0001'`, region `'NORTH'`, and the account's identifier, active status, current balance, credit limit, cash credit limit, open date, expiration date, reissue date, current-cycle credit and debit totals, address ZIP, and group identifier, then write the assembled record to the export output data store.
REQ-F-008

[State-driven] While records remain in the cross-reference input data store, the system shall read each card cross-reference entry sequentially and emit one cross-reference export record per entry until the end of the cross-reference input data store is reached.
REQ-F-009

[Event-driven] When a card cross-reference entry has been read from the cross-reference input data store, the system shall assemble an export record with record type `'X'`, the shared run timestamp, the next sequence number, originating branch `'0001'`, region `'NORTH'`, and the card number with its associated customer identifier and account identifier, then write the assembled record to the export output data store.
REQ-F-010

[State-driven] While records remain in the transaction input data store, the system shall read each transaction record sequentially and emit one transaction export record per transaction until the end of the transaction input data store is reached.
REQ-F-011

[Event-driven] When a transaction record has been read from the transaction input data store, the system shall assemble an export record with record type `'T'`, the shared run timestamp, the next sequence number, originating branch `'0001'`, region `'NORTH'`, and the transaction's identifier, type code, category code, source, description, amount, merchant identifier, merchant name, merchant city, merchant ZIP, associated card number, originating timestamp, and processing timestamp, then write the assembled record to the export output data store.
REQ-F-012

[State-driven] While records remain in the card input data store, the system shall read each card record sequentially and emit one card export record per card until the end of the card input data store is reached.
REQ-F-013

[Event-driven] When a card record has been read from the card input data store, the system shall assemble an export record with record type `'D'`, the shared run timestamp, the next sequence number, originating branch `'0001'`, region `'NORTH'`, and the card's number, associated account identifier, CVV code, embossed name, expiration date, and active status, then write the assembled record to the export output data store.
REQ-F-014

[Ubiquitous] The system shall make the export input data store (`EXPORT-INPUT`) available for reading and all output stores — account output, card cross-reference output (`XREF-OUTPUT`), card master output (`CARD-OUTPUT`), customer output (`CUSTOMER-OUTPUT`), transaction output (`TRANSACTION-OUTPUT`), and error reporting store (`ERROR-OUTPUT`) — available for writing before any records are processed.
REQ-F-015

[State-driven] While records remain available in the export input data store, the system shall read each export record sequentially and dispatch it for type-specific processing until end-of-file is reached.
REQ-F-016

[Event-driven] When an export record is retrieved, the system shall inspect the record type indicator and route the record to the account handler when the type is `'A'`, to the customer handler when `'C'`, to the card cross-reference handler when `'X'`, to the transaction handler when `'T'`, to the card data handler when `'D'`, and to the unknown-record error handler for any other value.
REQ-F-017

[Event-driven] When an export record with type `'A'` is dispatched, the system shall copy every account attribute — identification, status, balances, credit limits, key dates, cycle totals, ZIP, and group identifier — from the export record into the account record and append the resulting record to the account output store (`ACCOUNT-OUTPUT`).
REQ-F-018

[Event-driven] When an export record with type `'C'` is dispatched, the system shall copy the customer identifier, first/middle/last name components, three address lines, state code, country code, ZIP code, two phone numbers, Social Security Number, government-issued identification, date of birth, electronic funds transfer account identifier, primary card holder indicator, and FICO credit score from the export record into the customer record, and write the resulting record to the customer output store (`CUSTOMER-OUTPUT`).
REQ-F-019

[Event-driven] When an export record with type `'X'` is dispatched, the system shall copy the card number, customer identifier, and account identifier from the export record into a new cross-reference entry and append it to the card cross-reference output store (`XREF-OUTPUT`).
REQ-F-020

[Event-driven] When an export record with type `'T'` is dispatched, the system shall populate a transaction record with the transaction identifier, type code, category code, source, description, amount, merchant identifier, merchant name, merchant city, merchant postal code, card number, original transaction timestamp, and processing timestamp from the export record, and append the resulting record to the transaction output store (`TRANSACTION-OUTPUT`).
REQ-F-021

[Event-driven] When an export record with type `'D'` is dispatched, the system shall map the card number, account identifier, CVV, embossed cardholder name, expiration date, and active-status indicator from the export record onto the card record and write it to the card master output store (`CARD-OUTPUT`).
REQ-F-022

[Event-driven] When an export record carries a record type indicator that is not one of the recognised values `'C'`, `'A'`, `'X'`, `'T'`, or `'D'`, the system shall compose an error entry containing the detection timestamp, the offending record type, the record's sequence number, and the message `'Unknown record type encountered'`, and write it to the error reporting store (`ERROR-OUTPUT`).
reqN: [Unwanted] If the import job is interrupted after partial writes to any output store, the system shall not automatically roll back the partial output; restart behaviour is the responsibility of the operations team.
openQuestions: The fixed originating branch value `'0001'` and region value `'NORTH'` are stamped on every exported record regardless of the actual source of the data. Should these values be configurable per run, or are they permanently fixed constants? — Owner: business/data architecture team

The shared sequence counter increments across all five entity types within a single run. Should the counter reset to 1 at the start of each run, or does it carry over across runs? The rules do not specify the counter's initial value or persistence. — Owner: batch operations team

[Ubiquitous] The system shall open the transaction record data store for sequential reading before any maintenance records are processed.

[State-driven] While maintenance records remain to be processed, the system shall classify each record by its operation indicator, apply the corresponding action, and advance to the next record until the input feed is exhausted.
REQ-F-003

[Event-driven] When the next maintenance record is requested, the system shall read it from the transaction record data store; if no further records exist, the system shall set the end-of-input indicator to signal that processing is complete.

[Event-driven] When a maintenance record is read, the system shall route it to the add handler if the operation indicator is `'A'`, to the update handler if it is `'U'`, to the delete handler if it is `'D'`, to the skip handler if it is `'*'`, and to the default handler for any other value.

[Event-driven] When a maintenance record with operation indicator `'D'` is dispatched, the system shall remove from the transaction type data store (`CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE`) the row whose transaction type code (`TR_TYPE`) equals the record's reference number; no other rows shall be affected.

REQ-F-011

[Event-driven] When a record with operation indicator `'U'` is processed, the system shall replace the stored description for the transaction type whose type code matches the record's reference number with the new description supplied on the input record.

[Event-driven] When a record with operation indicator `'D'` is processed, the system shall remove the row from the transaction type data store whose type code matches the record's reference number, leaving all other rows unaffected.

[Event-driven] When a record with operation indicator `'*'` is processed, the system shall skip the record and apply no change to the transaction type data store.

reqF: REQ-F-001

[Ubiquitous] The system shall derive the authorization year, month, and day from the caller-supplied origination date by treating positions 1–2 as the year, positions 3–4 as the month, and positions 5–6 as the day.
REQ-F-002

[Ubiquitous] The system shall compute the authorization time by subtracting the caller-supplied packed authorization time from `999999999` and shall split the resulting nine-digit value into hour (positions 1–2), minute (positions 3–4), second (positions 5–6), and millisecond (positions 7–9) components.
REQ-F-003

[Ubiquitous] The system shall insert one row into the fraud authorization store (`CARDDEMO.AUTHFRDS`) carrying the card, authorization, merchant, amounts, response, match status, fraud action, account, and customer details, the reconstructed authorization timestamp formatted with `'YY-MM-DD HH24.MI.SSNNNNNN'`, and the current system date as the fraud report date.
REQ-F-004

[Event-driven] When the insert against the fraud authorizations store reports a duplicate-key outcome (SQLCODE = -803), the system shall invoke the fraud update step to update the existing fraud authorization row with the fraud action code and current report date.
REQ-F-005

[Ubiquitous] The system shall reconstruct the authorization timestamp key for an update by inverting the packed authorization time from `999999999`, splitting the origination date into year, month, and day components, splitting the recovered time into hour, minute, second, and millisecond components, and staging the card number, assembled timestamp, and fraud action code for the update operation.
REQ-F-006

[Event-driven] When updating an existing row in the fraud authorizations store (`CARDDEMO.AUTHFRDS`), the system shall set the fraud action code (`AUTH_FRAUD`) and the fraud report date (`FRAUD_RPT_DATE`) to the current date for the row identified by card number (`CARD_NUM`) and authorization timestamp (`AUTH_TS`).
REQ-F-007
[Event-driven] When the fraud analyst confirms the fraud review action on the pending-authorization view, the system shall restore the session context and route the request to the fraud-marking flow.
REQ-F-008

[Event-driven] When the fraud-marking flow is triggered for a selected pending authorization, the system shall read the authorization summary keyed by the account identifier from the authorization store; if the summary is not found or the authorization store is exhausted, the system shall set the end-of-authorizations flag.
REQ-F-009
[Event-driven] When the authorization summary is found, the system shall read the matching authorization detail segment keyed by the selected authorization key from the authorization store.
REQ-F-010

[Event-driven] When the authorization detail has been retrieved, the system shall invert the fraud indicator: if the current fraud indicator is confirmed fraud (`'F'`), the system shall set both the record's fraud indicator and the requested action to remove-fraud (`'R'`); otherwise, the system shall set both the record's fraud indicator and the requested action to confirm-fraud (`'F'`).
REQ-F-011

[Event-driven] When the fraud indicator has been toggled, the system shall delegate the fraud-status change to the fraud authorization service, passing the updated authorization record, account identifier, customer identifier, and requested action.
REQ-F-012

[Event-driven] When the fraud authorization service reports a successful update, the system shall rewrite the authorization detail segment in the authorization store with the fraud-service-returned authorization record carrying the toggled fraud indicator.
REQ-F-013
[Unwanted] If the fraud authorization service does not report success, or if the delegation does not complete normally, the system shall skip the rewrite of the authorization detail segment.
REQ-F-014

[Event-driven] When the purge job starts, the system shall capture the current date in Julian form and set the expiry-days threshold to the supplied runtime parameter value when that value is numeric, or to 5 days when the parameter is absent or non-numeric.
REQ-F-015

[State-driven] While pending authorization summaries remain to be processed and no processing error has occurred, the system shall retrieve each pending authorization summary in turn from the authorization data store, iterate over its associated authorization detail records, and stop when the end of the authorization data store is reached or an error occurs.
REQ-F-016

[Event-driven] When the orchestrator asks for the next pending authorization summary, the system shall read the next summary segment from the pending authorization store, signal that more summaries remain when the store returns status `'  '`, and signal end-of-authorization-data when the store returns status `'GB'`.
REQ-F-017

[Event-driven] When the system requests the next authorization detail segment under the current summary, it shall signal that more authorizations remain when the retrieval status is blank, and signal no more authorizations when the status indicates no more segments under the current parent or end of the pending authorization store is reached.
REQ-F-018

[Event-driven] When an authorization detail record has been retrieved, the system shall compute the detail's age in days by subtracting the authorization date (recovered by subtracting the stored date complement from 99999) from the current Julian date, and mark the detail as qualified for deletion when the computed age is greater than or equal to the expiry-days threshold.
REQ-F-019

[Event-driven] When an authorization detail record is marked qualified for deletion and its response code is `'00'` (approved), the system shall decrement the parent summary's approved authorization count by one and subtract the detail's approved amount from the parent summary's approved authorization amount.
REQ-F-020

[Event-driven] When an authorization detail record is marked qualified for deletion and its response code is not `'00'` (declined), the system shall decrement the parent summary's declined authorization count by one and subtract the detail's transaction amount from the parent summary's declined authorization amount.
REQ-F-021
[Event-driven] When an authorization detail record is marked qualified for deletion, the system shall delete that detail record from the authorization data store.
REQ-F-022

[Event-driven] When all detail records under the current authorization summary have been evaluated and the summary's approved authorization count has fallen to zero or below, the system shall delete the authorization summary record from the authorization data store.
REQ-F-023

[Event-driven] When an authorization detail record's computed age is below the expiry-days threshold, the system shall mark the detail as not qualified for deletion and leave the parent summary's approved and declined counts and amounts unchanged.
REQ-F-024
[Ubiquitous] The system shall open the root summary output file (output file 1 record data store) for sequential writing before any pending authorization summary retrieval begins.
REQ-F-025
[Ubiquitous] The system shall open the child detail output file (output file 2 record data store) for sequential writing before any pending authorization summary retrieval begins.
REQ-F-026
[State-driven] While the pending authorization database has not been exhausted, the system shall retrieve each pending authorization summary record in sequence from the authorization database.
REQ-F-027
[Unwanted] If the authorization database returns an end-of-database status (`'GB'`) during summary retrieval, the system shall cease retrieving further summary records and complete the unload run.
REQ-F-028

[Event-driven] When a pending authorization summary is successfully retrieved and its account identifier is numeric, the system shall write the summary record to the root summary output file (output file 1 record data store).
REQ-F-029

[Event-driven] When a pending authorization summary is successfully retrieved and its account identifier is not numeric, the system shall skip that summary record and write neither a root record nor any child detail records for it.
REQ-F-030

[Complex] While child detail processing is active for a numeric-account pending authorization summary, the system shall retrieve each authorization detail record belonging to that summary in sequence using a get-next-in-parent traversal of the authorization database.
REQ-F-031

[Event-driven] When a pending authorization detail record is successfully retrieved, the system shall combine the current account identifier with the retrieved detail record and write the combined record to the child detail output file (output file 2 record data store).
REQ-F-032

[Event-driven] When the authorization database returns a segment-not-found status (`'GE'`) during child detail retrieval, the system shall cease retrieving further child detail records for the current summary and advance to the next pending authorization summary.
REQ-F-033
[Ubiquitous] The system shall reset the database status after each child detail retrieval iteration so that a status from a prior retrieval cannot affect the outcome of the next retrieval.
REQ-F-034
[Ubiquitous] The system shall make input file 1 (INFILE1) and input file 2 (INFILE2) available for sequential reading before any records are processed.
REQ-F-035

[State-driven] While input file 1 still has records to process, the system shall read each root pending authorization record sequentially from input file 1, place its contents into the pending authorization summary buffer, and insert it as a root segment into the hierarchical authorization database.
REQ-F-036

[Event-driven] When a root pending authorization summary record has been prepared for insertion, the system shall insert it as a root segment into the hierarchical authorization database using an unqualified root segment search argument.
REQ-F-037
[Event-driven] When input file 1 reports end-of-data, the system shall mark the root input source as exhausted and cease reading from input file 1.
REQ-F-038

[State-driven] While input file 2 still has records to process, the system shall read each child pending authorization record sequentially from input file 2 and, when the record's root segment key is numeric, load the root segment key into the qualified segment search argument, copy the child payload into the pending authorization details buffer, and proceed to parent verification before insertion.
REQ-F-039
[Unwanted] If a child pending authorization record's root segment key is not numeric, the system shall skip that record without inserting it into the authorization database.
REQ-F-040
[Event-driven] When input file 2 reports end-of-data, the system shall mark the child input source as exhausted and cease reading from input file 2.
REQ-F-041

[Event-driven] When a child pending authorization record is ready for insertion, the system shall verify that the referenced parent root segment exists in the authorization database by performing a get-unique lookup using the qualified root search argument carrying the child's root segment key.
REQ-F-042

[Event-driven] When the parent root segment lookup returns a blank status code confirming the parent exists, the system shall insert the pending authorization details record as a child segment beneath that root using an unqualified child segment search argument.
REQ-F-043
[Unwanted] If the parent root segment lookup returns a non-blank status code, the system shall skip insertion of the child pending authorization record.
REQ-F-044

[State-driven] While either input file 1 or input file 2 still has records to process, the system shall complete all root segment insertions from input file 1 before beginning child segment insertions from input file 2.
REQ-F-045

[State-driven] While pending authorization summary records remain available for extraction, the system shall sequentially retrieve each authorization summary record from the authorization database until the end of the summary collection is reached.
REQ-F-046
[Event-driven] When a pending authorization summary is successfully retrieved, the system shall proceed to validate and unload the summary along with its child detail records.
REQ-F-047

[Event-driven] When a retrieved authorization summary carries a non-numeric account identifier, the system shall skip that summary and all of its child authorization detail records without writing them to any output store.
REQ-F-048

[Event-driven] When a valid pending authorization summary is ready for unload, the system shall write the summary record to the parent output store and then iterate over all child authorization detail records belonging to that summary.
REQ-F-049
[Ubiquitous] The system shall retrieve each authorization detail record scoped to the currently established parent authorization summary, restricting retrieval to child segments of that parent only.
REQ-F-050
[Event-driven] When an authorization detail record is successfully retrieved, the system shall write that child authorization detail record to the child output store.
REQ-F-051
[Unwanted] If the authorization summary retrieval returns an end-of-database status (`'GB'`), the system shall terminate the summary iteration loop.
REQ-F-052

[Unwanted] If the authorization detail retrieval returns a no-more-children status (`'GE'`), the system shall terminate the child detail loop for the current parent authorization summary and return control to the summary iteration.
REQ-F-053
[Ubiquitous] The system shall clear the authorization retrieval status after handling each detail retrieval outcome before proceeding to the next retrieval.
reqN: [Event-driven] When the insert against the fraud authorizations store reports a duplicate-key outcome (SQLCODE = -803), the system shall invoke the fraud update step so the existing row is updated with the fraud action code and current report date.

[Event-driven] When the fraud authorization service confirms success, the system shall ensure that the rewrite of the authorization detail segment and the fraud-service-recorded status change are treated as a single consistent outcome — the detail segment is rewritten only after the service confirms success.

[Ubiquitous] The system shall write each valid pending authorization summary record to the parent output store and then write all child authorization detail records belonging to that summary to the child output store before advancing to the next summary.
openQuestions: Rule items describe stopping the purge loop when an error flag is raised, but no rule item specifies what constitutes an error condition or what action the system takes when one is detected (e.g., whether the job terminates, skips the record, or raises an alert). Clarification needed. — Owner: batch operations / authorization processing team

The rules state the summary is deleted when the approved authorization count falls to zero or below, but do not address the case where the declined count also falls to zero or below independently. Should a summary with zero or negative declined counts but positive approved counts also be deleted? — Owner: payment authorization domain team

The rules describe two separate output destinations — a root summary output file (output file 1 record data store) and a child detail output file (output file 2 record data store). It is not stated whether these files are truncated/recreated at the start of each run or appended to. Clarification is needed to determine restart behavior. — Owner: batch operations team

No rule describes handling for authorization database status codes other than blank (success), `'GB'` (end-of-database), and `'GE'` (segment-not-found). It is unclear whether unexpected status codes should cause the job to abort or be silently skipped. — Owner: payment authorization processing team
